result_summary: INCONCLUSIVE on the declared metric (arm 3). R(6J) = -0.0038 boot95 [-0.0331,+0.0255] vs benchmark B=+0.0331 and gate 0.60*B=+0.0198; the CI contains both 0 and the gate. Point estimate is -0.11x B, i.e. marginally INVERTED not merely attenuated. Design fault owned: B was the mean of 6E and 6B, and 6B's own contrast spans zero (+0.0073 [-0.0677,+0.0712]), so averaging a precise estimate with a null one made the gate noisier than assumed and forced arm 3. WHAT THE RUN DID ESTABLISH (post-hoc arms, labelled): H_clock WEAKENED -- R(6E)-R(6J) = +0.0627 [+0.0103,+0.1107] CI excludes zero, and 6J's per-slot rank profile agrees with 6E/6B (+0.283/+0.489) LESS than they agree with each other (+0.646); crude block-volume H_liquidity ALSO WEAKENED -- 6J's ny_pm has identical CME volume intensity to 6E/6B's (0.82x vs 0.80x/0.82x) yet 2-3x their reversion, so total contract volume is NOT the operative liquidity measure. The mechanism behind finding C is therefore OPEN. POST-HOC pattern logged as IDEA-0008 (not promoted): every product's strongest reversion sits in the block where the COUNTER CURRENCY's home market is shut -- 6E/6B in asia (London night), 6J in ny_pm (Tokyo night) -- and the overlap cell, where both home markets are open, is near-identical on all three (-0.0153/-0.0159/-0.0151). Premise and gates passed: 6J asia/overlap liquidity ratio 0.314 vs 0.129/0.132 (2.40x as declared); rule-9a clean on a never-before-loaded archive, Asia rv coverage 0.867 vs 6B 0.703; rule-23 reproduction of 6E/6B exact to 4dp and byte-identical. New: per-product reporting unit (6J = 1e-6 = $12.50, NOT the conventional USD/JPY pip) and 6J tick halving 1e-6->5e-7 mid-2015 verified against the price grid. Not tradable: 6J is ~19x under its cost floor ($0.65/bet vs $12.50 round trip), worse than 6E.
